finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /users throws a TypeError because req.pg is never set; the async handler has no try/catch, so on Express 4 with Node >= 15 the rejection is unhandled and one request terminates the process (service-wide DoS). Conditional: under Express 5 it returns 500 instead. Severity HIGH is conditional on Express 4 and Node >= 15, both unverified (no package.json in repo).
finding.source: Anonymous HTTP GET /users?org=<any> reaching db.js:8 (public ingress via app.listen(3002) at db.js:23, all interfaces)
finding.sink: req.pg.query(...) at db.js:9 inside async handler with no error handling; unhandled promise rejection

trace.note: app.listen(3002) with no host argument binds all interfaces; route is public ingress
req.pg is undefined (never assigned in repo); req.pg.query throws TypeError, producing a rejected promise
res.json never reached; no try/catch or .catch to convert rejection into a 500

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch or .catch on the handler; no error-handling middleware; no middleware assigning req.pg in the repo. Express version and Node runtime not verifiable (no package.json or lockfile). Validation: curl -i 'http://<host>:3002/users?org=x' (Tier 0); not executed.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only guard in the file is the path check at db.js:15, which is on the /file route and does not protect /users. No try/catch or .catch wraps the handler at db.js:8-11, no error middleware is registered, and a repo-wide grep finds no assignment to req.pg (only the read at db.js:9).
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: app.listen(3002) with no host at db.js:23 exposes the route, the async handler at db.js:8 reads req.pg.query at db.js:9 with req.pg never set in the repo, and res.json at db.js:10 is skipped with nothing catching the rejection. The anonymous request therefore always fails at db.js:9; whether that becomes a 500 (Express 5) or a process crash (Express 4 on Node >= 15) depends on package.json, which is absent, so the HIGH severity and DoS impact remain conditional while the defect itself is confirmed.

finding.claim: /users has no authentication or tenant binding; the caller-supplied org query parameter selects which organization's users are returned, so any anonymous client can enumerate user id and name across all organizations. Severity MEDIUM (bounded info disclosure of IDs and names); depends on no auth middleware existing outside this repo.
finding.sink: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1 at db.js:9, serialized to JSON at db.js:10

trace.note: GET /users route with no auth middleware in the route definition
req.query.org taken directly from the request and bound as $1 in the query
all matching id and name rows returned as JSON to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query ($1) prevents SQL injection; no authentication, session, or authorization check exists in db.js; no tenant derivation from a trusted identity. Not verified against any external auth middleware.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers app.get("/users") with no middleware. db.js:9 binds req.query.org as $1, which prevents SQL injection but is not an authorization check. db.js:10 returns all matching id and name rows. The only other app-level code (db.js:13-21) has no shared auth middleware, and there is no app.use() anywhere in the repo. The only file in the repo outside .claude/ is db.js, so no auth layer exists in this codebase.
verdict.reason: An anonymous client can call GET /users?org=<any> and receive id and name for that org's users, since db.js:8-10 has no authentication or tenant check; the parameterized query at db.js:9 stops SQL injection but not this cross-tenant disclosure. The one caveat is that a gateway or proxy outside this repo could add auth, which the candidate already flagged and which I cannot check from here, but nothing in the repo provides it.
